segmentName: Steam, Air & Hot Water Thermal Utility Solutions

market.worldSizeUSD_B_range: India steam trap market: $178.8M (2025) to $280.7M by 2034 (~4.99%/yr, one source cites 7.2%/yr). Global steam trap market estimates vary widely by vendor scope: $4.57B (2024) to $5.57B (2029, 4.1%/yr); $4.8B (2025) to $9.27B (2035, 6.8%/yr); or a narrower $971M (2023) to $1,259M (2030, 3.65%/yr). A related but much larger 'closed steam condensate recovery device' market is cited at $102.4B (2025) to $126.9B (2029) — not directly comparable, vendor market-boundary definitions differ substantially.
market.domesticSlice: Asia-Pacific holds ~41-45.6% share, the fastest-growing region. Forbes Marshall (India, private, family-owned) and Thermax Limited (India, listed) are the direct India-based peers; Thermax posted ₹10,640 Cr FY25 revenue (+14% YoY), ~11.5% 3-yr average ROE.

structureFacts: Rising industrial energy-efficiency and decarbonization mandates are pushing demand for steam trap monitoring, condensate recovery, and waste-heat recovery
Technology shift from manual steam-trap inspection to IoT/automated monitoring is a clear premiumization/service trend in the category
India-specific PLI or steam-equipment scheme was not confirmed this pass; general industrial energy-efficiency push (PAT scheme, BEE mandates) is the likely structural driver

adoptionStructure.note: Energy cost reduction, regulatory/ESG compliance pressure, uptime/reliability in process industries (textile, pharma, food, power), total cost of ownership vs. upfront equipment price, and increasingly digital monitoring/predictive-maintenance capability drive purchasing.
